absent: Locking and concurrency rules for descriptor tables, virtual machine control state, and layout globals.
Internals of emulation helpers, triage, perform access, unhandled handling, and identifier emulation.
Full contents, ordering, and reset values of the global register and instruction tables.
Derivation of hypervisor address width, DRAM bounds, and physical to virtual offset use.
Distributor read path, interrupt state machine, and virtual CPU control lifecycle.
User space access paths, visibility decisions, and sanitised register ranges.
Trace event definitions, payloads, and emission conditions.
Spectre capability detection, preamble size, and vector layout details.
True random operational behavior beyond version and result codes.

findings.text: AArch64 system trap handling records the exception syndrome and target general register, emits a trace, consults a triage helper that can claim the trap early, decodes the syndrome into operation fields, loads the associated general value, chooses between the register table and the instruction table based on whether the first operation field denotes a system register, performs the described access, writes the result back only for reads of system registers, and always reports the trap as handled.

Generic thirty two bit coprocessor handling obtains the target register index, copies that general value into the parameter block, attempts emulation against a caller supplied descriptor table, on success writes the possibly updated value back for reads and reports handled, otherwise invokes the unhandled access helper and still reports handled.

Thirty two bit CP fifteen handling decodes the syndrome into coprocessor fields, reroutes two narrow identifier ranges toward the sixty four bit identifier emulator, namely the first operation zero plus first control zero with either nonzero second control or second operation six, and first operation one plus first control zero plus second control zero plus second operation seven, and otherwise delegates to the generic thirty two bit path with the CP fifteen table.

Sixty four bit CP fifteen and CP fourteen handlers delegate to a shared sixty four bit helper with their respective tables, and the thirty two bit CP fourteen handler decodes the syndrome and delegates to the generic thirty two bit helper with the CP fourteen table, all reporting handled through the delegated path.

Parameter block carries five small operation and control selectors plus a sixty four bit value slot and a write flag, serving as the decoded form of either an exception syndrome or an architectural encoding for subsequent emulation.

Descriptor carries a debug name, an AArch thirty two mapping selector with direct low and high variants, five operation selectors, an optional trapped access callback, a reset callback, an index into saved state with zero meaning no storage, a value or mask word, optional user get and set callbacks with generic fallback, and an optional runtime visibility callback.
Runtime visibility overrides use bit zero for hidden from guest and user, bit one for read as zero in both, and bit two for writes ignored from user only.

True random interface uses version 65536, success 0, not supported unsigned minus one, invalid parameter unsigned minus two, no entropy unsigned minus three, and a maximum of 192 for sixty four bit requests.

Thirty two bit syndrome decoding extracts first operation from bits fourteen to sixteen, first control from bits ten to thirteen, second control from bits one to four, second operation from bits seventeen to nineteen, and treats cleared low bit as write.
Encoding helper builds a parameter block by splitting an architectural encoding into its five operation selectors through dedicated extractors, leaving value and direction to the caller.
Reset helper requires a nonzero storage index below the system register count, stores the descriptor value word into that slot, and returns the stored slot content.
Descriptor lookup compares an incoming encoding key against a candidate descriptor encoding by subtraction, yielding zero on match and signed ordering otherwise.

Descriptor construction helpers provide per field initializers for the mapping and five selectors, a full system descriptor derived from an encoding with stringified name, and a CP fifteen variant that forces direct mapping and zero for the first operation while deriving the remainder from the encoding.

Identifier register debug iteration walks the global descriptor table in order, skips entries that are not virtual machine feature identifiers, selects by zero based position among the survivors, yields nothing until the initialized flag is set, advances position on each step with no teardown, and on display prints the descriptor name with the current virtual machine identifier value as sixteen hex digits.

Reserved bits debug iteration walks the same global table, keeps only entries whose storage index reaches the sanitised start, selects by position, yields nothing until the mask table exists, advances position on each step with no teardown, and on display prints the name with separate sixteen digit hex masks for zero required and one required bits obtained from a per register query.

Early hypervisor address conversion keeps only low bits below a computed boundary and inserts a precomputed tag above that boundary, providing a reversible kernel to hypervisor mapping before full page tables.

Layout initialization chooses the hypervisor region as the opposite top bit from the identity map address, derives the tag boundary from the highest differing bit across the DRAM range, builds a low mask, optionally mixes random bits into spare high bits when randomization is enabled, normalizes the tag, and then derives the physical to virtual offset from a known hypervisor text symbol.

Relocation application walks a table of thirty two bit self relative offsets, resolves each to a linear alias address, reads a kernel image virtual address there, converts it through the early mapping, and writes the hypervisor address back.

Address translation patching expects five slots, replaces them with no operations on virtualization host extensions or after the first slot when the tag is zero, otherwise emits mask then rotate then two staged adds then inverse rotate using the registers decoded from the original slots, and faults if any emission fails.

Vector hardening patching expects four slots, does nothing without the relevant Spectre capability or warns on host extensions, otherwise computes the hypervisor vector address, merges low program counter bits to select the same vector, skips a preamble, and emits a three part move plus indirect branch.

Sixty four bit constant loading expects four slots, reuses the destination register from the original slot, emits zeroing move plus three keeping moves for successive sixteen bit pieces, and is used to materialize the kernel image offset and the sanitised cache register.

Interrupt controller restore validates requested priority width plus one against the stored per CPU width, identifier width against stored width, and system error and version bits against host capabilities, rejecting mismatches, otherwise updates the stored widths and forwards only binary point control and end of interrupt mode through the virtual machine control structure.

Virtual machine control setting dispatches on the distributor model, selecting version five, version three, or for version two choosing version three handling when the global CPU interface indicates version three else version two, and faults on unknown models.

Version two packing stores group enables plus acknowledge control plus fast interrupt enable plus binary point control plus end of interrupt mode plus alias and main binary points plus shifted priority mask into the legacy control word. Version three packing stores the same logical fields into the newer control word with fixed fast enable set and acknowledge cleared for native version three. Version five packing stores only priority and enable into a sixty four bit word.

Failure paths include assertion on zero or out of range storage index during reset, invalid argument on oversized or mismatched interrupt control restore, fatal fault on unknown distributor model, fault on unexpected patch slot counts or unencodable translation steps, and silent delegation to an unhandled helper for unmatched coprocessor encodings while still reporting handled.
Tracing headers define include guards and identify the trace system as kvm with current directory include path and matching include file names for ARM and exit handling.

Public initializers and setters exposed for other units comprise layout computation, relocation application, translation and vector patching, image offset and cache register materialization, and virtual machine control installation for all interrupt versions.
Public trap entry points exposed for dispatch comprise AArch sixty four system handling and CP fourteen and CP fifteen thirty two and sixty four bit handling.
